summary: This is a curated awesome-list (not a library) documenting 80+ browser automation tools across categories: traditional tools (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, Cypress), AI-powered automation (Browser-Use, Skyvern, Steel Browser, CamoFox), and related utilities (Cheerio, jsdom, node-crawler). The repo is a GitHub Pages-style markdown index with zero implementation code — it provides discovery and comparison value only. I verified the README is purely a categorized link directory with brief descriptions; CONTRIBUTING.md defines curation standards; there is no package.json, no source code, no API surface. The "Sponsored by CoreClaw" banner suggests commercial affiliation but doesn't affect list neutrality.

maturityAssessment.claimedMaturity: No maturity claims about the list itself — it's a living document. The sponsored CoreClaw claims 'Production-ready Web Data APIs' but that's an external service ad.
maturityAssessment.contradictionFlags: None — the README makes no false claims about being a library or having an API. It accurately presents itself as a curated list.

apiSurface: No API surface. This is a static reference document. Users consume by reading the README on GitHub or cloning the repo.
integrationPoints: Useful as a research reference for Veridian to discover candidate tools (Playwright, Browser-Use, Steel Browser, CamoFox, Libretto, Skyvern) but cannot be integrated programmatically. The list itself provides zero pipeline connectivity — it's a decision-support artifact, not a component.
strengthsForVeridian: Excellent discovery resource: consolidates the modern browser automation landscape including AI-agent tools that are directly relevant to Veridian's scraping pipeline (Browser-Use for AI-driven navigation, Steel Browser for sandboxed sessions, CamoFox for anti-bot evasion, Libretto for script generation). Actively maintained with 2026 additions. Unbiased categorization (AI vs traditional vs related).
weaknessesForVeridian: Zero executable code, no API, no programmatic access, no versioning, no quality signals (stars, maintenance status) embedded in the list — requires manual vetting of each candidate. The CoreClaw sponsorship may bias visibility. Not a library; cannot be depended on in package.json.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
